name: Clay C. Clark
childhood_experience: Given up for adoption; raised by neighbors
notable_stories: Son of Mary Frances Vantine given up for adoption; raised by neighbors
Adopted by the family living next door to John Wesley Adams's family; lived prosperously and raised his own family. The preparer believes he has found Clay's descendants.
milestones: Owned 80 acres in Township 56 North, Range 19 West, northwest Chariton County, Missouri, beside G. P. Allen (plat map, about 1880)
career: Clay became a very successful cattle rancher and served several terms in the Oregon Legislature.
sources: Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, compiled by William W. "Bill" Allen (2 April 2011 edition)
Family research emails, 2011–2013 (John and Barbara Adams with Irma Kulp Zacher, George F. Adams, Bill Allen and others)
Plat map of Township 56 North, Range 19 West, Chariton County, Missouri (about 1880), highlighted by Bill Allen
notes: Half-sibling of John Wesley Adams' children. Born 1860. Given up for adoption.
The Willett family, neighbours on the Chariton County map, adopted or raised Clay until he turned 18. [Family research emails, email 4]
Unconfirmed: Around 1883 Clay moved to Arlington, Oregon, on the Columbia River. [Family research emails, email 04]

Open question: Mary Frances Vantine (Adams): she married Ephraim Clark at 15 and was barely 16 when he died at the end of the Civil War (1865), which conflicts with her tree birth of Oct 1844 and with Clay C. Clark's tree birth of 1860. [Family research emails, email 15, 16, 04]

The Willett family, who raised Clay until he was 18, owned 160.58 acres (W. W. Willet) in the upper right of the same township on the plat map of about 1880. [Plat map of Township 56 North, Range 19 West, Chariton County, Missouri (about 1880), highlighted by Bill Allen]
